title: Canonical open tensor and scalar comparison data
statement: Let j:U→X be an open immersion of schemes and φ:A→B a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use the ordinary unbounded constant-module derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact open extension and restriction of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], the tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the fixed scalar left adjoints of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Fix the ordinary restriction/scalar isomorphism sectionwise, and descend it by the exact derived functors. Define q by uniqueness of the composite scalar/open left adjoints. Define r as the inverse scalar-adjunction mate of that descended restriction/scalar isomorphism. Then this fixed mate r is invertible. The ordinary and derived projection maps are the published adjunction mates; the exact-restriction tensorator is the published derived tensor comparison. Flatness and K-flatness mean [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and [def-pc-kflat-complex] after the canonical constant-module realization of [lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat]. The degreewise scalar representative normalization predicates use these same fixed functors and the adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction].

proof.text: Use the published open restriction/upper-star comparison. The two composites of sectionwise restriction and the restriction/coextension scalar adjunctions have equal units: naturality of the module restriction/coextension unit is exactly the sectionwise equality. Identify the inverse ordinary square with the canonical upper-star/scalar square by uniqueness of left adjoints.

The exact derived square respects symmetry. Transport its inverse scalar mate along the published identification L(j-star) ≅ D(j-star). The generic mate-transport equation follows by expanding the units and counits and applying naturality.

Apply the étale part of scalarPullbackReverse_isIso in [lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-mate]. The transported mate is its composite with isomorphisms, so is invertible. This proves invertibility of the fixed map, rather than existence of some comparison isomorphism.

theorem openScalarRestrictionMap_isIso
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    IsIso (openScalarRestrictionMap φ j)
